events.title: Salt and Soil at Steam Next Fest — the demo is out now
events.summary: Hi! Roman here.Salt and Soil is taking part in Steam Next Fest, and I'd like to invite you to try the free demo. It follows the first thirty years of one family's life near Jamestown, from 1607 to 1637: a homestead of your own, neighbours, hard years, and decisions around the family table.Since the playtest, I've reworked the scenario and the graphics, and brought much more life to the map: people and wagons travel along the roads, ships sail the rivers, and settlements have more detail. events.title: The Continent, Redrawn — and a New Playtest in September
events.summary: Hi! Roman here.I've spent the last few weeks in the mountains — the in-game ones, that is. Salt and Soil has a new map: I rebuilt both the way it is rendered and the data it is built from.A new look. The map is now one continuous landscape: mountains have slopes, shadows and snowy peaks, rivers wind through valleys, the coastline feels alive, and forests and plains change with the climate.More accurate geography. events.title: We're in! Salt and Soil has entered the DevGAMM Awards 2026
events.summary: I'm happy to share that Salt and Soil: A Frontier Family Sim has been accepted to participate in the DevGAMM Awards 2026.This means the game has officially entered the competition — it is not a nomination yet. events.title: The first playtest wave is complete — thank you!
events.summary: Thank you to everyone who joined the Salt and Soil playtest, guided a family through its first decades in Jamestown, and shared their thoughts.What made me happiest was hearing that, for some players, the family tree became a real reason to keep going: you wanted to see who would survive the hard years, who would become the next head of the family, and what would happen to the children once they grew up. events.title: The Free Steam Playtest Is Now Open
events.summary: The free Steam Playtest for Salt and Soil is now open. The playtest includes Jamestown Chronicle, a 30-turn scenario following the early life of one frontier family near Jamestown, beginning in 1607. Manage the household’s limited labor, secure food and materials, build the homestead, trade with the people around you, and face Family Council decisions shaped by your situation.
